title: Rabbi David Tawil: Life Lessons From Pirke Abot- "Is Our Stuff Blocking Us from Happiness?"

chapters.title: The Endowment Effect in Psychology
chapters.about: Jean Piaget and how children and adults develop ownership attachment.

chapters.title: Memories, Heirlooms, and Self-Worth
chapters.about: Why people hold onto old items like dining sets and photo albums.

chapters.title: A Torah Perspective on Possessions
chapters.about: Connecting the Ten Commandments, stealing, and human essence.

chapters.title: Giving and Letting Go
chapters.about: Using donations and charity to overcome hoarding and attachment to stuff.

chapters.title: The Illusion of Material Happiness
chapters.about: Hillel's teaching on possessions and how buying things masks deeper needs.

chapters.title: Finding True Contentment and Peace
chapters.about: Focusing on Torah, Sedaka, simplicity, and inner peace.

summary: Rabbi Tawil explores the psychological and emotional attachment people develop toward their material possessions and how this ties into self-worth. Drawing on psychological studies and Torah concepts, he discusses how materialism can hinder true happiness and how focusing on giving, Torah, and simplicity leads to genuine contentment.
questions: Why do people get so attached to things they own?
What is the connection between stealing and taking Hashem's name in vain?
How does materialism affect our pursuit of true happiness?
Why can giving Sedaka help people let go of possessions?
How does simplicity bring more peace and time into our lives?
